title.narrative: Recognize, Protect, Empower: Towards a National Policy for the Protection of Sex Workers in Sri Lanka

description.narrative: This project aims to promote the recognition, protection, dignity, and human rights of sex workers in Sri Lanka through the development and advocacy of a National Policy for the Protection of Sex Workers. The project is based on a human rights, labour rights, and gender equality approach and seeks to address the legal, social, and structural barriers that prevent sex workers from accessing justice, protection, healthcare, social services, and equal treatment. Sex workers in Sri Lanka continue to face stigma, discrimination, violence, harassment, social exclusion, and legal vulnerabilities. Existing laws and policies do not adequately protect their rights, and they are often excluded from decision-making processes that directly affect their lives. As a result, many sex workers experience barriers in accessing essential services, legal protection, and social security. This project seeks to address these challenges by ensuring that sex workers themselves play a central role in developing policy solutions that reflect their lived realities and needs. The overall objective of the project is to develop and advocate for the adoption of a comprehensive National Policy for the Protection of Sex Workers in Sri Lanka. The project has four specific objectives: 1. To generate evidence on the challenges, protection needs, and policy gaps affecting sex workers through participatory consultations and research. 2. To develop a rights-based National Policy for the Protection of Sex Workers through a consultative and inclusive process. 3. To strengthen the participation and leadership of sex workers in policy development and advocacy processes. 4. To advocate for policy reforms and government adoption of the National Policy to improve protection, access to justice, and social inclusion.
